Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 66
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: South Eastern Asian
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Roofer
  trauma_type: Toxic chemical exposure
  pcl5: 36

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Nighttime/Dark: Night-time or waking up in the dark, Olfactory (Hospital): Hospital or antiseptic smell, Olfactory (Smell): Related smells
  Maladaptive Strategies: Past Dwelling: I dwell on how I used to be before the event, Avoid Assertiveness: never disagree or assert myself to avoid conflict, Suppress Thoughts: try hard not think about the trauma
  Threat: Cannot Relax: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place, Concentration: Having difficulty concentrating, Avoid Unfamiliar Places: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
  Memory: Memory Replay: My memories of the frightening event are like a film that plays over and over., Emotion Without Image: Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory, Vivid Memory: My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed.
  Negative Appraisals: Can't Rely on Self: I can't rely on myself, Hopelessness: I have no future, World is Dangerous: The world is a dangerous place

Vignette:
Sokhon, a 66-year-old South Eastern Asian man, had spent most of his life working as a roofer, taking pride in his physical strength and ability to provide for his family. But everything changed on that fateful day when he was exposed to toxic chemicals while working on a construction site. The smell of the chemicals still lingered in his mind, transporting him back to that moment of utter chaos. As Sokhon recounted the event, his eyes would glaze over, and his voice would trail off. He remembered feeling disoriented, unable to breathe, and collapsing onto the ground. His coworkers rushed him to the hospital, where he spent several days recovering. The antiseptic smell of the hospital still haunted him, and even a whiff of something similar could send him spiraling back into that dark place. After the accident, Sokhon began to withdraw from his daily life. He found himself dwelling on how things used to be before the exposure, remembering the ease with which he would climb roofs and work long hours without complaint. His wife noticed the change in him, but whenever she tried to talk to him about it, Sokhon would brush her off, avoiding any conflict or assertiveness that might stir up unwanted emotions. As time passed, Sokhon's avoidance behaviors became more pronounced. He stopped taking on new roofing projects, fearing unfamiliar places and the potential dangers they posed. At home, he would become agitated if his wife tried to get him to go for a walk or engage in any activity that involved leaving their neighborhood. "What if I have an attack?" he would say, his voice laced with anxiety. Sokhon's inability to relax was evident even when he was sitting in the safety of his own living room. His mind would wander back to the accident, replaying the events like a film on repeat. He couldn't shake off the feeling that the world was a treacherous place, waiting to pounce on him at any moment. At night, Sokhon's memories of the event would resurface with vivid clarity, making it impossible for him to sleep. The darkness seemed to amplify his fears, and he would lie awake, convinced that something terrible was lurking just outside his window. His wife tried to reassure him, but Sokhon couldn't rely on himself or others; in his mind, everyone and everything had the potential to let him down. Sometimes, without warning, Sokhon would feel an intense emotional surge, like a tidal wave crashing over him. He wouldn't be able to pinpoint why it happened or what triggered it – all he knew was that the world seemed to be spinning out of control. His wife described these episodes as "the darkness descending," and they left her feeling helpless. One evening, as Sokhon sat in his living room, staring blankly at the TV, his wife took his hand and said, "You need help, Sokhon. You can't keep living like this." For a moment, he considered resisting, but something about her words struck a chord within him. He looked up at her, his eyes filled with tears, and whispered, "I'm lost. I don't know how to find my way back." It was then that Sokhon realized he needed help to break free from the grip of his traumatic memories and rebuild his shattered sense of self. As he stood up, a glimmer of determination flickered within him – a spark that would ignite the journey towards healing and recovery.
